explain: _ille_ is “that” (the one over there) for masculine nouns. It follows the same pattern as _hic_.
distractors: _illum_ is accusative. A subject needs the nominative: _ille_.

explain: _illa_ is “that” for feminine nouns. _fēmina_ is feminine, so _illa fēmina_.
distractors: _illam_ is accusative. A subject needs the nominative: _illa_.

explain: _illud_ is the neuter “that”. Like _hoc_, it can stand alone to mean “that thing”.
distractors: _ille_ is masculine (“that man”). “That” on its own, a thing, is neuter: _illud_.
_illa_ is feminine. “That” as a thing is neuter: _illud_.
_illum_ is masculine accusative. A subject needs the nominative: _illud_.

explain: The man is the thing seen: _virum_ and _illum_ are accusative.
distractors: _ille_ is nominative. The thing seen is accusative: _illum_.
_illī_ is dative (“to that”). The thing seen is accusative: _illum_.

en: The sword of that man is good.
explain: _illīus_ is the genitive of _ille_ for every gender (“of that”). It sits with _virī_ (genitive).
distractors: _illum_ is accusative. “Of that man” is genitive: _illīus_.
_illī_ is dative (“to that”). “Of that man” is genitive: _illīus_.
_ille_ is nominative. “Of that man” is genitive: _illīus_.

en: I give a book to that woman.
explain: _illī_ is the dative of _ille_ (“to that”). The woman receives the book, so _illī fēminae_ and _librum_ (accusative).
distractors: _illam_ is accusative. The one receiving is dative: _illī_.
_illa_ is nominative. The one receiving is dative: _illī_.
_illīus_ is genitive (“of that”). The one receiving is dative: _illī_.

en: This man is good, that man is bad.
la: Hic vir bonus est, ille malus.
explain: _hic_ points to what is near, _ille_ to what is far. Together they mean “this one … that one” (or “the latter … the former”).
distractors: Hic vir bonus est, illa malus.
Hic vir bonus est, illud malus.
Hic vir bonus est, illum malus.
_illum_ is accusative. A subject needs the nominative: _ille_.

explain: For “he, him, she, her, it” Latin uses _is, ea, id_. The thing seen is accusative, so “him” is _eum_.
distractors: _is_ is nominative (“he”). The thing seen is accusative: _eum_.
_eī_ is dative (“to him”). The thing seen is accusative: _eum_.

explain: _eam_ is the feminine accusative of _is, ea, id_: “her” as the thing seen.
distractors: _ea_ is nominative (“she”). The thing seen is accusative: _eam_.
_eius_ is genitive (“of her”). The thing seen is accusative: _eam_.

explain: _eius_ (“of him, of her, of it”) is how Latin says “his” or “her” when it means someone else’s: _fīlium eius_, the son of him.
distractors: _eī_ is dative (“to him”). “His” is the genitive: _eius_.

explain: _eōs_ is the masculine plural accusative of _is_: “them” as the things seen.
distractors: _eī_ is nominative plural (“they”). The things seen are accusative: _eōs_.
_eās_ is “them” for women. For men, use _eōs_.
_eīs_ is dative or ablative (“to them”). The things seen are accusative: _eōs_.
